standing_doctrine: Burden of proof is on the CANDIDATE trigger, not the incumbent (CLAUDE.md Rule 1/OP-16 eval-first). A missed setup is not itself evidence a new trigger is profitable -- the study must show the candidate's NEW-episodes-only population clears real A/B expectancy under honest friction, not merely that it would have caught today's bar. Kill = current exact-pierce semantics stand; no shame in a null result (OP-22).

motivating_incident.root_cause: backtest/lib/filters.py#detect_level_rejection requires bar.high > level (exact pierce). J's HTF+ribbon bear alignment was intact but the setup never registered because SPY never touched 747.88/748.42 to the penny -- it rejected FROM BELOW. Prior art: detect_wick_rejection_bearish (filters.py, added 2026-05-10 after the same miss class on J's 2026-04-29 10:25 entry) already tolerates the PIERCE side (bar reaches/exceeds the level, closes back below by up to WICK_CLOSE_TOLERANCE). The APPROACH side -- price gets close but never reaches the level at all -- has NO trigger of any kind today. This study builds and tests that missing mirror.

external_context._doc: WebSearch, 2026-07-17, ~20 min, bounded per task instruction. Grounds the Z parameter GRID below -- our own real-OPRA data decides the verdict, these claims never gate a pass/fail.

claims.claim: A common ATR-based S/R zone-width method adds a fraction of ATR -- commonly 0.25x ATR -- to the zone boundary so a level test has 'breathing room' without materially widening risk.
claims.source: ATR Based Support and Resistance, TrendSpider Store (https://trendspider.com/trading-tools-store/indicators/68ebfc-atr-based-support-and-resistance/)

claims.claim: ATR-derived zone width automatically adapts to market volatility, vs. a fixed-price zone which does not; markets rarely react from one exact tick because orders/liquidity/prior positioning are distributed across a range.
claims.source: Support and Resistance: Identifying S/R with Average True Range, FasterCapital (https://www.fastercapital.com/content/Support-and-Resistance--Identifying-Support-and-Resistance-with-Average-True-Range.html)

claims.claim: Common practitioner guidance places stops 0.5-1.0x ATR beyond an S/R zone to absorb normal volatility and avoid stop-hunts (brief piercing wicks before reversal) -- a related but distinct convention from zone-width itself, cited here only to bound the ATR-multiple order of magnitude in use.
claims.source: Support and Resistance Trading: Complete Guide for Futures, Optimus Futures (https://optimusfutures.com/blog/support-and-resistance-trading-guide/)

claims.claim: A percentage-band convention (e.g. 1%, 2%, 5%, 10% off a level) is used to study price reaction near round levels; crypto practice commonly uses smaller Fibonacci-flavored bands (1.0%, 1.618%, 2.0%...).
claims.source: Support and Resistance Zones | Trading Key Levels, AlphaEx Capital (https://www.alphaexcapital.com/stocks/technical-analysis-for-stock-trading/price-action-and-chart-patterns/support-and-resistance-zones)

claims.claim: Illustrative practitioner framing: a stock 'holding $45 support' may actually bounce from $44.70 or $45.40 -- think '$44.50-$45.50' rather than '$45.00 exactly' -- i.e. an example tolerance band on the order of +/-$0.50 around a round equity level.
claims.source: Support and Resistance Levels Explained, StockAlarm (https://pro.stockalarm.io/blog/support-resistance-levels-guide)

claims.claim: Round-number levels (multiples of $5/$10/$50) attract genuine order-flow clustering from options market-maker hedging and algorithmic orders, not merely trader psychology -- supporting zone (not surgical-price) treatment of round/strike-adjacent levels such as SPY's own strike grid.
claims.source: 0DTE SPY Options Strategy synthesis, TradeAlgo / journalplus S/R guide (https://www.tradealgo.com/trading-guides/options/0dte-spy-options-strategy ; https://journalplus.co/strategies/support-resistance-trading/)

claims.claim: Treating S/R as zones rather than single lines is reported to reduce false breakout signals and improve entry timing versus a strict single-line convention.
claims.source: Support and Resistance Zones: Why Areas Beat Exact Price Levels, The Bull (https://thebull.com.au/trading-guides/support-resistance-zones/)

claims.claim: A hybrid pivot-candle-structure + ATR-volatility-cap method is used by some indicator implementations specifically to prevent one unusually large candle from blowing out an otherwise-reasonable zone width -- i.e. ATR should cap, not solely define, zone size.
claims.source: Dynamic ATR Cluster Support Resistance Zones, TradingView / tradingbauhaus (https://www.tradingview.com/script/OMUh7f5y-Dynamic-ATR-Cluster-Support-Resistance-Zones/)

external_context.grid_derivation: Fixed cells {15c,30c,50c,75c,$1.00} bracket the practitioner illustrative range (~$0.50-$1.00 example tolerance on SPY-scale prices) while adding a tighter half (15c/30c) since SPY 0DTE precision is much finer than the $45-stock illustration. ATR-relative cells {0.1x,0.2x,0.3x}xATR(14,5m) are set BELOW the commonly-cited 0.25x-1.0x ATR range found above -- deliberately conservative, since a level-REJECTION entry trigger (this study) is a materially different mechanism from a stop-placement buffer (what most of the found sources describe); starting tighter and letting the data decide whether even the conservative end clears is the eval-first-appropriate choice, not an attempt to manufacture a pass.

hypothesis.statement: Adding a proximity-band REJECTION trigger -- bar.high within Z of a resistance-role level from BELOW (level - Z <= bar.high < level, i.e. never pierced) AND a red close (bar.close < bar.open) AND no pierce/wick trigger already fired that bar -- to the SAME 'level_rejection' trigger slot filters.py already feeds (mirroring the wick-promotion pattern, filters.py evaluate_bearish_setup 'elif wick_level is not None:' branch) adds POSITIVE-EXPECTANCY entries under SS-B exit shape + honest friction, on the NEW-episodes-only population (episodes the current exact-pierce trigger does not already catch), for at least one Z cell on at least one account.
hypothesis.falsifiable_prediction: If TRUE: at least one Z cell's NEW-episodes delta population clears all 5 ratification gates + BH-FDR on Safe and/or Bold. If FALSE: no Z cell clears on either account -- KILL, current pierce-only semantics stand, and today's 10:15 incident remains an accepted miss (a setup existing but ungated is not automatically a profitable trigger).

z_grid.atr_definition: ATR(14) on SPY 5m bars, True Range = max(high-low, abs(high-prev_close), abs(low-prev_close)), simple rolling mean over 14 bars, continuous across day boundaries (no explicit overnight-gap reset) -- disclosed convention, not the only valid one.
z_grid.red_close_requirement: bar.close < bar.open (plain red bar) -- required on ALL cells, fixed and ATR-relative alike; not itself swept (out of this grid's scope, follow-up candidate if the base mechanism clears).
z_grid.mutual_exclusion_with_existing_triggers: The candidate fires ONLY when neither the existing pierce trigger (detect_level_rejection) NOR the existing wick trigger (detect_wick_rejection_bearish) already fired that bar -- guarantees the candidate never overlaps/reclassifies an episode the engine already catches; it is additive only.

control.definition: Current exact-pierce behavior -- backtest/lib/filters.py#detect_level_rejection UNMODIFIED (bar.high > level AND close < level). Equivalent to Z=0 / candidate disabled.
control.note: No file edit to filters.py is made to produce this control -- it IS the current, already-shipped, unmodified function. mining_method_umbrella._doc: Efficiency device, disclosed: instead of 8 separate full-history orchestrator runs per account (16 total), ONE candidate mining pass per account is run with an UMBRELLA Z = max(1.00, 0.3*ATR_at_bar) -- a per-bar dynamic value guaranteed >= every grid cell's threshold (fixed max=$1.00, ATR-relative max=0.3x). Every zone-branch fire is logged with its exact (level, proximity_cents = level-bar.high, atr_at_fire). Each of the 8 grid cells is then a POST-FILTER of this one umbrella episode set (membership: proximity_cents <= Z_dollars for fixed cells; proximity_cents <= Z_frac*atr_at_fire for ATR-relative cells) -- smaller Z is by construction a subset of the umbrella set for the SAME bar-level trigger condition.
mining_method_umbrella.pierce_preservation: The candidate detector calls the ORIGINAL unmodified detect_level_rejection first and returns its result unchanged if non-None -- guarantees every bar where the pierce trigger already fires behaves IDENTICALLY (same level, same bar) in both control and candidate runs, so already-covered episodes cannot be miscounted as new.
mining_method_umbrella.known_path_dependence_caveat: Because the umbrella run uses the WIDEST Z, it could in principle occupy a position slot on a bar that a STRICTER, per-cell-only run would not have entered on, altering what happens later that day in a way a true isolated per-cell run might not reproduce exactly (state-machine ripple: setup_quality_taken_today / re-entry locks are path-dependent on entry order). This is a disclosed, accepted simplification -- NOT independently verified per cell. It biases toward the umbrella set being a slight OVER-approximation of a true isolated per-cell mine in edge cases, never an under-approximation for the smallest cells' membership test itself (proximity_cents is recorded exactly per fire, so which EPISODES qualify per cell is exact; only the DOWNSTREAM SAME-DAY SEQUENCING after a wide-Z entry is the disclosed approximation).

episode_attribution._doc: Per the task's explicit requirement: the delta is the NEW-entries-only population, explicit about attribution -- reuses WF-GATE-METHODOLOGY-2026-07-16.md's own matched-episode delta_i definition.
episode_attribution.episode_key: (date, direction) slot, matched by ORDINAL position within that day's bear-entry sequence (1st bear entry of the day in control matched to 1st bear entry of the day in candidate, etc.) -- a disclosed simplification when a day's entry COUNT differs between control and candidate (it can, since an earlier zone entry may pre-empt or unlock a different later sequence).
episode_attribution.unchanged: candidate ordinal-matched entry has IDENTICAL entry_ts to control's -- delta_i = 0 by construction, NOT replayed (saves the OPRA-fetch+SS-B-replay cost; the pierce-preservation guarantee above makes this safe).
episode_attribution.new: candidate has an entry in an ordinal slot control has none for that date -- delta_i = pnl_candidate(episode) - 0, per WF-GATE-METHODOLOGY's own rule for one-side-only episodes. This is the PRIMARY population (today's incident's exact shape: a day with zero bear entries under control that gets one under candidate).
episode_attribution.shifted: both control and candidate have an entry in the same ordinal slot but at DIFFERENT entry_ts (candidate's zone trigger fired before control's later pierce trigger that same underlying level-test) -- delta_i = pnl_candidate(episode) - pnl_control(episode), BOTH sides independently replayed through the IDENTICAL SS-B lineage (never orchestrator's own internal P&L, which is a legacy/uncertified exit model) so the comparison is apples-to-apples.
episode_attribution.metadata_recovery: Each new/shifted episode's proximity_cents/atr_at_fire is recovered by matching the trade's entry_time_et against the umbrella run's zone-branch fire log (exact timestamp match, else nearest logged fire within 10 minutes). Unrecoverable metadata (should be rare/zero given the fire log covers every zone-branch evaluation) is counted (n_metadata_unrecovered) and excluded from per-cell membership, never imputed.

ratification_gates._doc: Per CLAUDE.md OP-16 + WF-GATE-METHODOLOGY-2026-07-16.md (Fable, frozen 2026-07-16), the FROZEN A/B-delta WF form -- read and applied, not re-derived. ALL FIVE required for a cell to be ship-ready, per account, independently (C29).
ratification_gates.1_oos_positive: sum(delta_i for episodes with date >= oos_start) > 0.
ratification_gates.2_wf_ge_070: WF_delta = (sum_oos(delta_i)/n_oos) / (sum_is(delta_i)/n_is) >= 0.70, computed ONLY when is_delta_mean > 0 (frozen verdict ladder). is_delta_mean <= 0 and oos_delta_mean <= 0 => FAIL. is_delta_mean <= 0 and oos_delta_mean > 0 => INSUFFICIENT_REGIME_SHIFT (park per AMENDMENT 1's re-test trigger, not auto-ratified, not a clean pass).
ratification_gates.3_sub_window_stable: OOS delta episodes split chronologically in half (sw1/sw2, same both_halves convention every SS-B-lineage study this week used); <=1 of {sw1,sw2} negative.
ratification_gates.4_anchor_no_regression: None of the 7 CLAUDE.md OP-16 J-anchor trades' own (date,direction) ordinal slot is touched by this candidate (checked directly -- anchors already fire via their own existing triggers; a candidate that is additive-only per mining_method_umbrella.pierce_preservation cannot alter an anchor's OWN entry unless the anchor's day also contains an independent NEW/SHIFTED zone episode on the SAME direction, checked explicitly, not assumed).
ratification_gates.5_evidence_n_advisory: n (deduped new+shifted episodes, post exclusions) >= 15 is ADVISORY (OP-16) -- a thin-n PASS ships if the other 4 gates clear, labeled thin, not hidden.
ratification_gates.control_sanity_disclosure: Per WF-GATE-METHODOLOGY's mandatory disclosure: a null/control sanity check is computed alongside every real cell -- the SAME delta machinery applied to a RANDOM zone-fire population (random_entry_null, seeded, drawn from the account's own entry gate) to confirm the gate is discriminating (if the sanity cell also 'passes', wf_not_discriminating=true is flagged and the verdict rests on the remaining gates with the anomaly disclosed, per the frozen note).
ratification_gates.bh_fdr_correction: Benjamini-Hochberg step-up across all 8 Z cells x 2 accounts = up to 16 test statistics this run, alpha=0.10, one-sided normal-approximation p-value for mean(delta_i) > 0 -- same algorithm as backtest/autoresearch/ribbon_rejection_wick_battery.bh_fdr / FDR_ALPHA, reused unchanged (the house convention every study this week used). A cell failing the BH-FDR cut does NOT auto-ship even if conditions 1-5 nominally clear.

decision_rule.statement: Per account, independently: a Z cell is SHIP-READY iff it clears all 5 ratification_gates AND survives BH-FDR. If >=1 cell is ship-ready on an account, the WINNER is the cell with the highest OOS delta expectancy per trade (tie-break: larger n). SHIP timing is separately gated on real clock time (et_clock.py) -- no filters.py edit before 16:00 ET regardless of study verdict (mid-session engine-edit doctrine, CLAUDE.md). If a winner exists, default ON for Safe per J's directive IF Safe's own cohort independently clears (C29) -- Bold ships independently only if BOLD'S OWN cohort clears, never inherited from Safe's result.
decision_rule.kill_criterion: If NO Z cell clears on EITHER account: KILL. Current exact-pierce semantics in filters.py#detect_level_rejection stand UNCHANGED. The scorecard reports the Z cell that came CLOSEST (most gates passed, or least-negative OOS delta) and names which specific gate(s) failed it -- an honest miss stays an honest miss; today's 10:15 incident is logged as an accepted gap, not silently retried.
